narr: A large upper trough shifted southeast into the Four State Region on August 21st through the 22nd, along the backside of an upper level low pressure system over the Great Lakes. This trough slowed as it entered the region, and interacted with rich Gulf moisture and available heating to help focus scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across the area. Given the weak steering currents aloft, these thunderstorms were slow moving and were very efficient rainfall producers, which resulted in flash flooding across several areas in East Texas, where widespread rainfall amounts of three to six inches fell with isolated higher amounts over seven inches.
ev: Holly Road washed out in one area due to flooding.
Flooding reported on County Road 1513 and County Road 1560.
Flooding forced the closure of North Phillips Spring Road, with several vehicles stranded in the high water.
